subject: Post-call: performance contract questions and reporting playbook
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@medsoft.io>, IT Ops <ops@medsoft.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: performance targets + next steps

Thanks for the sync earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move toward contract language. I kept this focused on measurement/SLAs since procurement wanted the concrete pieces.

Agreed/clarified items from the call:
- Non-streaming (request-response) latency target: p95 <= 120 ms, measured server-side (ingress -> final token emitted).
- Streaming: initial token latency target p95 <= 300 ms; customer requests we validate streaming tail behavior (p99) separately — see note below.
- Throughput: target baseline ~500 reqs/s with ability to burst to 750 for a short window.
- Concurrency: effective concurrency target for the service path: 150 concurrent active sessions.
- Measurement approach: server-side timestamps (ingress timestamp and final token flush). We'll exclude client network time and rendering.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows, provider-instability (upstream), and verified DDoS incidents. We need to define cold-start exclusion windows per deployment variant.

What Redwood will deliver next:
1) A draft SLO/SLA excerpt with precise measurement language and exclusion windows (attached: redwood_slo_draft_v2.pdf).
2) A short reporting playbook: report cadence (monthly automated report + weekly alerts for thresholds), sample dashboards, and how we'll surface incidents.
3) Example telemetry we will collect (latency histograms, top endpoints, sample traces); Ben will propose credit formulas.

Your asks / open items we need from MedSoft:
- Confirm whether p99 tail for streaming must be contract-level (you mentioned p99 <= 1s as a desired cap) or only an operational guide.
- Share top-5 endpoints and representative payload sizes (so we can validate kernels/batching assumptions).
- Procurement: do you have a required remediation cadence for incidents (48 hrs SLA on root cause identification?)

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood (Ben/Karthik): finalize SLO draft + propose remedies and credit sizing (ETA: 48 business hours).
- MedSoft (Sofia/Procurement): send endpoints + sample payloads; indicate whether streaming p99 should be a contractual metric (ETA: EOD Monday).
- If this looks good we can steer to legal for drafting DocuSign terms.

Thanks — attaching the draft SLO for your review.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_slo_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 185 KB)]

From: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@medsoft.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Ops <ops@medsoft.io>, Procurement <procurement@medsoft.io>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets + next steps

Thanks Dylan — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming tail: we do need a contractual p99 cap. Target is p99 <= 1.0s for streaming end-to-end token latency for our real-time transcription endpoint. If you can propose measurement semantics that exclude client-side network variability, that works.
2) Reporting: monthly export of the full histogram for top-5 endpoints + a weekly automated alert if p95 degrades more than 25% vs baseline.
3) Remedies: procurement expects credit formulas tied to monthly uptime and latency breaches. Please propose a sample cap; we prefer a sliding scale (0.5% credits per violation up to a 10% cap).

Attaching the stream profile CSV (payload sizes and typical session lengths) so you can sanity-check throughput assumptions.

Sofia Moreno
Head of Platform Ops | MedSoft Health
[Attachment: medsoft_stream_profiles.csv (csv, 12 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 07:48:00 -0800
Subject: internal: suggested contract adjustments before legal

Quick internal notes after Sofia's reply — share these in the SLO draft before legal: 
- Keep streaming p99 contractual but define clear measurement methodology: use the server-side last-byte emittance timestamp; require MedSoft to provide representative sessions for validation.
- Remedies: propose sliding credits but cap at 5% for first-year customers (protects us while we stabilize).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance window default = 30 minutes per calendar month; emergency maintenance carveout up to 2 hours for critical remediations.
- Cold-start: define a 10-minute warm-up exclusion after deploy/scale events for dedicated pools.
- Reporting cadence: monthly automated report + quarterly joint review (include raw histograms for top endpoints).

I'll draft the credit tiers and paste into the SLO doc. Karthik, can you add the exact telemetry keys we will export?

—Ben

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@medsoft.io>, Procurement <procurement@medsoft.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets + next steps

Thanks Sofia — incorporating Ben's notes. Pasted below is the proposed SLO excerpt we'll include in the contract; please confirm acceptance or flag edits so we can route to legal.

--- SLO excerpt (contract-ready) ---
Scope: Applies to Redwood-managed inference endpoints provisioned for MedSoft Health under deal MSH-2026-Q4-0921.
Measured metric: Server-side request latency measured from ingress timestamp to final token emission. Client network time is excluded.
Targets:
- Non-streaming: p95 <= 120 ms measured across monthly aggregation.
- Streaming (real-time transcription): initial token p95 <= 300 ms; streaming tail p99 <= 1.0 s for end-to-end server-side token latency.
Throughput and concurrency: Baseline capacity = 500 reqs/s with guaranteed minimum concurrency of 150 sessions. Short bursts to 750 reqs/s supported for at most 10 minutes per incident.
Exclusions:
- Scheduled maintenance (default 30 minutes/month).
- Emergency maintenance (up to 2 hours for critical fixes).
- Verified third-party provider outages and confirmed DDoS events.
- Cold-start exclusion: 10-minute warm-up for pool scale-up or deployment.
Reporting cadence:
- Monthly automated SLO report with histograms for top-5 endpoints.
- Weekly threshold alerts (configurable) for p95 deviations >25% vs baseline.
Remedies:
- Sliding credit scale, sample proposal attached, capped at 5% monthly credit for year one.

[Attachment: slo_excerpt.txt]

If acceptable, I will hand to legal this afternoon. If you want a higher credit cap or different exclusion windows, flag them now and we'll negotiate.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@medsoft.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsoft.io>, IT Ops <ops@medsoft.io>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance targets + next steps

Appreciate the quick turn. We accept the SLO excerpt with two minor asks:
1) Add an annual SLA review clause (we want a joint architecture review once per 12-month period).
2) In DocuSign, show the credit table and indicate escalation contacts.

Procurement confirms 12-month term + provisioning lead times (we'll include that in the commercial sheet). Please route to legal and DocuSign when you're ready.

Sofia
Head of Platform Ops | MedSoft Health
[DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/sign/abc-verify-link]
